extracted.intended_audience: attachers (broadband providers), utilities (pole owners), and counsel/FCC staff handling pole attachment disputes
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria governing requests for RBAT review, staff-supervised mediation, placement on the Accelerated Docket, and utility disclosure of pole inspection information in connection with pole attachment applications affecting broadband deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to request RBAT review
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT review and assessment process is available only to attachers and pole owners that are direct parties to such dispute (including any legal counsel retained to represent a party in that specific dispute). For matters to be considered for inclusion on the Accelerated Docket, a prospective complainant must notify the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau’s Market Disputes Resolution Division (MDRD) by phone and in writing prior to filing the formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial notification by phone and in writing constitutes the notification required under 47 CFR § 1.736(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for RBAT Review and Assessment form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A streamlined form (Request for RBAT Review and Assessment) will be used and will elicit information relevant to the scope and nature of the dispute and whether it is appropriate for expedited mediation and/or placement on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form will require: parties and services identified; section(s) of the Act or rule/order alleged violated; brief description of the dispute and how it relates to broadband deployment plans or projects (including deadlines, whether in unserved/underserved area, harm occurring or likely, and aspects requiring immediate redress); specific relief sought; whether parties have an NDA; steps taken to resolve matter; whether parties are amenable to mediation; whether the party intends to seek Accelerated Docket inclusion; and suitability info (e.g., number of poles, number/complexity of claims, likely need for discovery or expert affidavits). RBAT may request additional information as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT scheduling and fact-gathering authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a completed Request, the RBAT will schedule a meeting, with all parties, as soon as practicable and may request written responses or documentation from either party relevant to the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In initial or subsequent meetings, RBAT will provide guidance on resolving disputes (staff-supervised mediation, Accelerated Docket, other actions), attempt to distill disputed issues, identify the most impactful/urgent issues, encourage focusing on threshold issues or 'test cases' to narrow disputes, and may encourage streamlining the proceeding where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT recommendation and complainant acceptance procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT may recommend placement of a dispute on the Accelerated Docket; a prospective complainant may accept the recommendation, with or without the consent of the other party, by moving forward with the agreed upon schedule and process established by Commission staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exercise of discretion is consistent with Commission staff authority under 47 CFR § 1.736(d) and the complainant acceptance under § 1.736(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation procedures and confidentiality (section 1.737)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff-supervised mediation shall be conducted pursuant to 47 CFR § 1.737, and the strict confidentiality requirements of § 1.737(f) apply to all written and oral communications prepared or made for purposes of such mediation (Mediation Communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediation submissions, offers of compromise, and staff and party comments during mediation may not be used or disclosed in Commission proceedings or before other tribunals unless compelled by law. The MDRD Chief, in consultation with RBAT, may modify or waive procedures of § 1.737 for good cause and to serve the public interest (see 47 CFR § 1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT authority to require mediation or pre-filing settlement negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although mediation is generally voluntary, the RBAT may require that the parties participate in pre-filing settlement negotiations or mediation under § 1.737 as a condition for including a matter on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is authorized by 47 CFR §§ 1.736(e) and 1.737(a). The Commission declined to make the 180-day deadline trigger on RBAT request because successful mediation obviates the need for complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT authority to send matters to ALJ for expedited minitrial
rubrics_metrics.description: If RBAT determines a matter is suitable for inclusion on the Accelerated Docket, it may send appropriate matters to the Commission’s Administrative Law Judge for an expedited 'minitrial' (trial-type hearing) as contemplated by 47 CFR § 1.736(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RBAT may use this path for expedited adjudication when suitable given the issues and time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality-of-factors determination for Accelerated Docket placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT will decide whether a complaint or portion of a complaint is suitable for inclusion on the Accelerated Docket based on the totality of specified criteria (not automatically for an entire category of disputes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because strict time constraints apply in Accelerated Docket cases, RBAT must carefully evaluate suitability on a case-by-case basis to protect due process and ensure fair adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: claim within Commission jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the prospective complainant states a claim for violation of the Act or a Commission rule or order that falls within the Commission’s jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a threshold eligibility consideration to ensure the Commission can adjudicate the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: expedited resolution likely to advance broadband deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the expedited resolution of a particular dispute or category of disputes appears likely to advance the deployment of broadband facilities, especially in an unserved or underserved area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on impact to deployment goals; priority to disputes where prompt resolution will materially aid buildout in priority areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: exhaustion of settlement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the parties to the dispute have exhausted all reasonable opportunities for settlement during any staff-supervised mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RBAT should ensure parties have made sufficient effort to resolve or narrow disputes before Accelerated Docket inclusion; RBAT may require mediation as condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: number and complexity of issues in dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: The number and complexity of the issues in dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High numbers/complexity may make 60-day or similar Accelerated Docket deadlines inappropriate; RBAT must weigh this in suitability assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: whether dispute raises novel issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the dispute raises new or novel issues versus settled interpretations of rules or policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New/novel issues may require more time and careful consideration, reducing suitability for expedited disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: likely need for and complexity of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The likely need for, and complexity of, discovery in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive discovery needs weigh against Accelerated Docket placement given the short deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: likely need for expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The likely need for expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expert affidavits/testimony are necessary and complex, expedited timelines may be inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: ability of parties to stipulate to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of the parties to stipulate to facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater ability to stipulate supports suitability for expedited resolution; lack of stipulation ability may complicate meeting tight deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: whether parties have assembled relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the parties have already assembled relevant evidence bearing on the disputed facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evidence is already assembled, disputes are more likely suitable for expedited disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: willingness to seek rulings on subset/test cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The willingness of the prospective complainant to seek a ruling on a subset of claims or issues (e.g., threshold or 'test cases').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focusing on representative test cases can have broader impact and facilitate streamlined resolution of multiple similar disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: other RBAT-discretionary factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Such other factors as the RBAT, within its discretion, may deem appropriate and conducive to the prompt and fair adjudication of the complaint proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria are holistic; no single factor is dispositive and RBAT may consider additional case-specific elements to protect due process and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and potential additional streamlining
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will closely monitor the impact of the adopted dispute resolution procedures and consider additional streamlining measures if it observes ongoing delay tactics or other unreasonable practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy may be revisited based on observed practical outcomes to better enable broadband deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide cyclical/periodic pole inspection reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities must provide to potential attachers, upon request, the information contained in their most recent cyclical pole inspection reports, or any intervening periodic reports created before the next cyclical inspection, for the poles covered by a submitted attachment application, including whether any affected poles have been 'red tagged' and scheduled replacement date/timeframe (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to increase transparency and help attachers plan deployments; applies where the state has not certified regulation of pole attachments to the state (see State Regulation Public Notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: cyclical and periodic pole inspection reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A cyclical pole inspection report is any report created in the normal course of business that sets forth results of routine inspections during the utility’s normal inspection cycle; a periodic pole inspection report is any report created in the normal course of business that sets forth results of inspection outside the normal cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes utilities already prepare such reports in many cases; the rule requires provision only of information they already possess and track in inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of pole inspection information request and utility response
rubrics_metrics.description: When asking for pole status information for a planned buildout, the attacher must submit its information request no earlier than contemporaneously with an attachment application; the utility will have ten business days to respond to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ten business days is intended to allow time before the make-ready survey for the attacher to revise or amend its application as appropriate. The utility also has ten business days to determine whether the application is complete (47 CFR § 1.1411(c)(1)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention obligation for pole inspection reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities are required to retain copies, in whatever form created, of any cyclical or periodic pole inspection reports they conduct in the normal course of business until the utility completes a superseding cyclical pole inspection report covering the poles included in the attachment application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This retention duty is limited to reports the utility already creates; utilities are not required to collect new information solely to respond to such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended application and option to restart the 45-day review period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a utility receives an amended attachment application prior to granting or denying the original application, the utility has the option to restart the 45-day period for responding on the merits and conducting the survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities electing to restart the 45-day period must notify the attacher within 5 business days of receipt of the amended application or by the 45th day after the original application is considered complete, whichever is earlier. The Commission encourages attachers to file amended applications quickly and utilities to use the restart option judiciously and review amended applications promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of additional survey costs after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional survey costs necessitated by an amended application (e.g., a second survey) will be borne by the new attacher consistent with the attacher’s obligation to pay for make-ready costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 47 U.S.C. § 224(i) and 47 CFR § 1.1408(b) as authority for cost allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities not required to create new information
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requires utilities to provide only the information they already possess and track in the normal course of conducting pole inspections; it does not require utilities to collect or create new information solely for responding to such requests or to provide all information they may possess outside their inspection reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation is intended to balance transparency needs against burdens on utilities. The record shows many utilities do not maintain detailed maintenance/replacement schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling sensitive/confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent inspection reports may include sensitive or confidential network or financial information, utilities and attachers should address disclosure issues via redactions or non-disclosure agreements; the new rule is not intended to override laws precluding disclosure of certain information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may use NDAs or redactions; utilities expected to work in good faith to provide available information consistent with legal constraints (e.g., Protected Critical Infrastructure Information regulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability limitation based on state certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility disclosure requirement applies only in states that have not certified that they regulate pole attachments themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See State Regulation Public Notice, 37 FCC Rcd 6724; where states have regulatory certification, the federal disclosure mandate does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible RBAT information-request approach (rejection of rigid respondent list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts a flexible approach where the RBAT may request relevant information and documentation from either party as appropriate rather than specifying rigid, pre-prescribed respondent information requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required information in a response will depend on the complainant’s allegations; Commission found a rigid specification impracticable and prefers RBAT discretion to tailor requests.
